up1:0.2: Verses on the Blessings of Success
up1:1.1: ° Māra, the terrible one, who had created a thousand arms with weapons,
up1:1.2: and had mounted on (the elephant) Girimekhala, with his army,
up1:1.3: did the lord of sages defeat by such things as generosity and so forth -
up1:1.4: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!
up1:2.1: ° Even more terrible than Māra was the impatient and obdurate yakkha Ālavaka,
up1:2.2: who fought (with the Buddha) throughout the whole night,
up1:2.3: (him) did the lord of sages defeat by his patience and self-control
up1:2.4: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!
up1:3.1: The great elephant Nālāgiri, who was completely intoxicated,
up1:3.2: fearful, like a jungle fire, a flaming discus, or a flash of lightning,
up1:3.3: did the lord of sages defeat by sprinkling (him) with the waters of friendliness -
up1:3.4: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!
up1:4.1: With a sword that was lifted high in his outstretched hand, that very fearsome (bandit)
up1:4.2: the one with a finger necklace (Aṅgulimāla) ran for (the whole of) three leagues up the path:
up1:4.3: (him) did the lord of sages defeat with the psychic powers created in his mind -
up1:4.4: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!
up1:5.1: Having made her midriff (look large) with a piece of wood, like one who is pregnant,
up1:5.2: Ciñcā (then spoke) wicked words in the midst of a group of people:
up1:5.3: (her) did the lord of sages defeat by means of his gentleness and peacefulness -
up1:5.4: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!
up1:6.1: The arrogant Saccaka, who had given up the truth, and had challenged (the Buddha) to a debate,
up1:6.2: with his mind fixed on his argument, completely blind to the truth,
up1:6.3: (him) did the lord of sages defeat with the shining lamp of true wisdom -
up1:6.4: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!
up1:7.1: ° Taming the wise dragon Nandopananda, who had great power,
up1:7.2: by way of his son (Moggallāna), who was a dragon of an elder,
up1:7.3: (thus) did the lord of sages defeat (him) by instructing (his son to use) psychic power -
up1:7.4: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!
up1:8.1: He whose hand was badly bitten by the serpent of wrongly taken up views,
up1:8.2: the brahma Baka, who was clear and bright, and who possessed psychic powers,
up1:8.3: did the lord of sages defeat with the medicine of his super-knowledge -
up1:8.4: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!
up1:9.1: ° He who recites these eight verses each and every day,
up1:9.2: which are about the Buddha’s (many) blessed successes, and remembers them with diligence,
up1:9.3: after giving up (all) the many and various kinds of adversity,
up1:9.4: that wise man will (soon thereafter) attain both freedom and happiness.
